title: [ORION-QG QG-7f] Final pinned-chain closure on the three-block pin graph
body:
Parent programme: #740
Last-link parent: QG-7d #836.
Earned sibling: J7 PA single-pinner all-n closure, PR #870, dual-harness GREEN.
State instrument: QG-22 #868 / PR #869, dual-harness GREEN (18-state exact hidden-home J5 quotient per phantom home).
Pending sibling: QG-7e #872 / PR #873, single-pinner PP all-hidden-environment confirmatory lane.

## Status

**REGISTERED FINAL-CHAIN FRONTIER — do not execute/freeze an outcome packet until QG-7e has an honest terminal.**

The remaining QG-7d obligation is no longer an amorphous `pinned comm-s2` sector. After J7 and, if positive, QG-7e, the only unclosed shapes are exactly those excluded by the original QG-7d chain gate:

1. one selected comm-s2 block has **two simultaneous pinners** among the other two TARE blocks; and/or
2. a pinner is itself **comm-s2**, producing a two-/three-block pin chain or cycle.

Because frozen R6M has exactly three blocks and QG-7c already proves frame support<=2 and Tag support<=2, this is a finite structural object.

## Key structural reduction to prove first

From the QG-7c M1 inventory, an irreducible comm-s2 block has both support coordinates occupied by the shared Tag. Since global Tag support is <=2, **all comm-s2 blocks in one configuration must use the same two Tag coordinates `{b,a}`** (up to order/relabeling).

Therefore chain growth cannot create arbitrarily many comm-s2 coordinates. Extra coordinates can arise only as phantom homes of non-comm-s2 pinners. With three blocks there are at most two such homes.

Strong target:

> Every remaining pinned-chain configuration can be represented on the two common Tag coordinates plus at most two phantom-home coordinates, with a finite directed pin graph on three block vertices.

This representation lemma must be machine checked before any normalization theorem.

## F1 — canonical pin-graph inventory

Define the pin relation from the exact QG-7c T4b semantics, not from a new informal graph rule. Canonicalize under block permutation and Tag-coordinate swap.

Required graph/shape census distinguishes at least:
- selected C with two non-C pinners (`A/P` combinations);
- C -> C chain with third block A/P;
- mutual two-C pinning with third A/P;
- three-C path/cycle where semantically realizable;
- mixed cases with one/two phantom homes.

Here `A/P/C` are the already-earned irreducible anchored / phantom / comm-s2 M1 shapes. No new block type may be introduced in V1.

## F2 — compose hidden-home quotients rather than raw 4^24 enumeration

Each phantom home carries the exact six-letter local environment studied by QG-22. Reuse only the **proved state map**, not its answer as an unverified shortcut:

- raw one-home domain 4096 -> 18 exact structural cells for the relevant home delta;
- at most two phantom homes -> at most `18^2=324` paired structural states before graph/visible constraints.

Generic ORION must independently verify that the QG-22 quotient remains sufficient when two home coordinates coexist; if cross-home F3 interactions arise, the product quotient is refuted and the missing coupling coordinate becomes the result.

## F3 — counterexample-first known-family discriminator

For every canonical chain state, compute a proof-carrying feasible reference and exact known-family costs/upper bounds:
- parent G1-G4 / J7-style whole-component relocations;
- exact D+;
- exact B′;
- exact B″ where type-correct.

If a feasible chain member has

`U_chain < min(C_Dplus, f_Bprime, f_Bsecond)`

then it is a genuine **fifth TARE support-two configuration/regime witness**. Preserve the first canonical strict row and stop theorem promotion; unrestricted DP is optional for the strict known-family separation.

No post-outcome B‴ definition is allowed in the same freeze.

## F4 — whole-component relocation theorem if no fifth regime

If the counterexample arm is negative, search a prospectively frozen joint exchange over the entire connected pin component, rather than repeatedly normalizing one pinner while recreating another.

Candidate measure remains the original QG-7d well-founded measure:

`M=(#comm_s2 blocks, #pinned comm_s2 incidences, Tag weight)` lexicographically.

A positive move must:
- be non-increasing in exact frozen unit cost for every canonical visible/hidden state;
- strictly decrease M;
- not create a new comm-s2 block or pin incidence outside the connected component;
- preserve exact shared labels/acceptance.

Allowed handoff after the joint move: already-earned D+/B′/B″ only.

## F5 — all-n composition

A complete finite chain inventory plus a move that strictly decreases M is sufficient to lift the local result to all n only if all spectator coordinates are proved inert/unchanged or carried by a complete local state quotient.

Finite n=3/n=4 absence alone may not authorize the theorem.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION:
- rebuild M1 A/P/C shape semantics and the pin relation independently;
- reconstruct the canonical graph census;
- independently validate QG-22 home-state composition or produce a cross-home counterexample;
- replay every known-family strict witness / normalization move from primitive Pauli/F3 rules.

Native ORION-Q keeps distinct:
- `CHAIN_REPRESENTATION_COMPLETE`
- `FIFTH_REGIME_WITNESS`
- `CHAIN_ALL_N_NORMALIZATION`
- `GLOBAL_BDOUBLEPRIME_COMPLETENESS`

No global B″ completeness until QG-7e (or its honest alternative) plus QG-7f both close and the complete QG-7c composition chain is rebound.

## Honest terminals

- `QG7F_CHAIN_REPRESENTATION_FINITE__NORMALIZATION_OPEN`
- `QG7F_FIFTH_SUPPORT2_REGIME_FOUND__PIN_CHAIN_WITNESS`
- `QG7F_PIN_CHAIN_CLOSED_ALL_N_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG7F_QG22_PRODUCT_STATE_INSUFFICIENT__CROSS_HOME_COUPLING_FOUND`
- `QG7F_PARTIAL__<obligation>_OPEN`
- `QG7F_CANNOT_CHECK`

## Claim boundary

Finite graph enumeration, state-product quotients, lexicographic descent and compiler-family optimization are donor methods. Candidate contribution is only the exact frozen TARE chain classification/theorem or counterexample. No novelty, R6 or physical quantum advantage.
